meta.task_prompt:
This repo's own README, in the "Status" section, flags a real gap: "there's no
authentication in front of the UI or API, so don't expose the collector
Service outside the cluster without putting your own auth in front of it."

Fix that. Add authentication in front of the collector's HTTP surface:

- The JSON/query API under `internal/collector/queryapi` and
  `internal/collector/ingest`.
- The server-rendered HTMX/Alpine UI under `internal/collector/ui`.

Use a simple, self-hosted scheme appropriate for a homelab project — a
token or basic-auth credential supplied via config/env, checked in
middleware — not an external OAuth provider. Wire it through the same
config mechanism the rest of the collector's settings already use (check how
existing ConfigMap-driven settings are read). Make sure the agent-to-collector
ingest path (`POST /api/v1/logs`) still works — that's service-to-service, not
a browser, so it likely needs its own credential rather than sharing the UI's.

This repo has real test coverage and a real convention for it. Match that
convention:

- Add table-driven `_test.go` files for the new middleware/auth logic, in the
  same style as the existing tests in `internal/collector/*`.
- Run `go test ./...`, `make vet`, and `make fmt` before finishing, and make
  sure all three are clean — don't declare the task done otherwise.
- Update `deploy/k8s/*.yaml` and the README/config docs if the new auth
  setting needs to be provided at deploy time.

When you are done, close with a single clear paragraph summarizing exactly
what you changed and why — that summary becomes the pull request's title and
body verbatim, so make it read like a real PR description, not an internal
note.

code_review.summary: The core of the change is solid: small, readable middleware in internal/collector/auth.go; constant-time credential comparison; a separate Bearer token for the agent ingest path; fail-fast validation in collector.New; health, ready and metrics endpoints left open for probes; and config wired through the existing flat getEnv convention. The problems are mostly at deploy time and at the edges of the design. The agent DaemonSet and collector Deployment now require a Secret without marking it optional, so the claimed 'opt-in, harmless no-op when disabled' behaviour is wrong for anyone who doesn't create that Secret. A placeholder Secret with 'changeme' credentials sits in deploy/k8s/, and the README's existing instruction to `apply deploy/k8s/*.yaml` will apply it as-is. AUTH_ENABLED fails open on any value strconv.ParseBool doesn't accept. The task explicitly asked for table-driven tests; auth_test.go is eleven near-identical standalone functions, and the PR body wrongly calls them table-driven. None of this is hard to fix, but the deploy-manifest issues should be fixed before merge.

findings.summary: The agent's AUTH_INGEST_TOKEN secretKeyRef (and the collector's envFrom secretRef at collector-deployment.yaml:39) isn't marked `optional: true`, so pods won't start if the tracer-collector-auth Secret is missing, even with AUTH_ENABLED=false.
findings.failure_scenario: An existing user upgrades by applying the changed DaemonSet/Deployment, or follows the new secret template's own advice to create the Secret out of band and skips collector-secret.yaml. Kubelet then reports CreateContainerConfigError: every agent pod on every node, plus the collector, stays down. That contradicts the manifest comment ('Harmless no-op when the collector has auth disabled') and the PR's 'default to disabled for backward compatibility' claim.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `optional: true` to the secretKeyRef in agent-daemonset.yaml and to the `secretRef` in collector-deployment.yaml. Missing credentials with AUTH_ENABLED=true are still caught by the fail-fast check in collector.New.

findings.summary: A Secret with working 'changeme' username/password/token is placed inside deploy/k8s/, which the README tells operators to `kubectl apply deploy/k8s/*.yaml` wholesale. The placeholder then gets deployed, and the non-empty check in New() accepts it.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator follows README's Deploying section (line 108, 'apply `deploy/k8s/*.yaml`') and then sets AUTH_ENABLED=true. The collector starts without complaint, protected by changeme/changeme, and anyone who guesses the default gets UI/API access and can inject logs via the ingest token. The warning comment inside the YAML is easy to miss when applying a glob.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the template out of the apply glob (e.g. deploy/k8s/examples/collector-secret.example.yaml) and document `kubectl create secret generic ...` in the README Auth section. Alternatively, make collector.New reject the literal placeholder value 'changeme' when AuthEnabled is true.

findings.summary: getEnvBool quietly falls back to the default (false) when a value doesn't parse, so AUTH_ENABLED fails open with no log or error.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator sets AUTH_ENABLED: "yes", "on" or "enabled" in the ConfigMap. strconv.ParseBool rejects it, getEnvBool returns false, and the collector serves the UI, query API and ingest with no auth, while the operator believes auth is on. The fail-fast validation in New never runs because AuthEnabled is false.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat a set-but-unparseable security toggle as a hard error: have Load return an error or record the raw value, and fail in collector.New when AUTH_ENABLED is non-empty but doesn't parse. At minimum, log a warning naming the rejected value.

findings.summary: The task explicitly required table-driven tests for the middleware, but auth_test.go is eleven copy-pasted standalone test functions, and the PR body says 'New table-driven tests cover both middlewares'.
findings.failure_scenario: This doesn't match the stated repo convention the task asked for, and the PR description misstates what was delivered. Adding a new credential case means copying another 12-line function.
findings.suggested_fix: Collapse into two table-driven tests, TestBasicAuthMiddleware and TestTokenAuthMiddleware, with fields {name, cfg, setupReq, wantCode, wantWWWAuth} and t.Run subtests, like TestNewReturnsErrorWhenAuthEnabledWithMissingCredentials already does. Correct the PR body.

findings.summary: The 'DifferentLength' tests say they verify timing-constant comparison, but they only assert a 401, so they're functionally duplicates of the wrong-credential tests.
findings.failure_scenario: Replacing secureCompare with a plain `==` would still pass all three tests, so the comment ('Ensures timing-constant comparison is used') gives false assurance.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the misleading comments and fold these into the table as ordinary wrong-credential rows, or add a small direct unit test for secureCompare's equal/unequal/different-length cases without claiming to test timing.

findings.summary: The `expectNoWWWAuth` table field is `true` in every row, so it's a dead dimension of the table.
findings.failure_scenario: Readers expect some row to exercise the false case. The field adds noise without adding coverage.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the field and assert unconditionally that token-auth 401s carry no WWW-Authenticate header.

findings.summary: Route-level tests leave gaps: POST /query/run, /logs/results, /trace and /trace/{id} are never checked unauthenticated; nothing checks that crossed credentials are rejected (Basic creds on ingest, Bearer on API); and there's no test for getEnvBool or the AUTH_* mappings in Load.
findings.failure_scenario: A future refactor could drop basicAuthMiddleware from POST /query/run, the one state-changing UI route that runs ad-hoc queries, or a typo could break an env var name, and CI would still pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the route table to every protected pattern, add rows showing Basic credentials get 401 on POST /api/v1/logs and a Bearer token gets 401 on GET /api/v1/logs, and add a small config_test.go using t.Setenv for AUTH_ENABLED/AUTH_* parsing, including an invalid bool.

findings.summary: The Bearer scheme check is case-sensitive (`strings.CutPrefix(..., "Bearer ")`), but RFC 7235 auth schemes are case-insensitive.
findings.failure_scenario: A non-tracer client, such as a curl script or another shipper, that sends `Authorization: bearer <token>` with the correct token gets a 401. The in-repo agent always sends 'Bearer', so there's no impact today.
findings.suggested_fix: Split on the first space and compare the scheme with strings.EqualFold(scheme, "Bearer").

findings.summary: When the agent's token is wrong or missing, the collector's 401 goes down the generic non-2xx retry path, so batches retry with backoff until the ring buffer drops them, with no distinct signal that the cause is auth.
findings.failure_scenario: If AUTH_INGEST_TOKEN differs between the agent and collector (e.g. the Secret was rotated on one side only), every node quietly loses logs. The only symptom is generic 'unexpected status 401' retry errors.
findings.suggested_fix: Special-case 401/403 in send() or Run(): log a clear 'ingest auth rejected — check AUTH_INGEST_TOKEN' message and/or increment a dedicated metric so the misconfiguration shows up quickly.

findings.summary: TestForwarderSendsAuthTokenInHeader and TestForwarderSendsNoAuthHeaderWhenTokenEmpty are 30-line near-duplicates that differ only in the token and the expected header.
findings.failure_scenario: Duplicated polling and server setup makes the file harder to maintain and again doesn't follow the requested table-driven style.
findings.suggested_fix: Merge into one table-driven test with rows {token: "secret-token", want: "Bearer secret-token"} and {token: "", want: ""}.

process_review.summary: The run followed a sensible pipeline: an ask agent surveyed the repo, the orchestrator handed the coder a precise spec, the coder implemented it in about 30 well-ordered tool calls, then tester and reviewer ran in parallel and a PR was opened. It cost about $1.55 over 108 turns and 153 tool calls, which is proportionate for a 15-file, +580-line change touching Go code, tests, manifests and docs. Every edit was preceded by a read of the same path, so there were no read-before-edit violations. The required checks really did run and passed in the trace: the coder ran `go test ./...` (line 146), `make vet` (line 150) and `make fmt` plus an explicit `gofmt -l` (lines 152 and 154). The tester re-ran all three after its own edits (lines 263 and 281). The tester also caught a gofmt problem it had introduced itself (line 253), which matters because `make fmt` is `gofmt -l` and exits 0 even when files need formatting. The main waste came from the ask agent, which ran `search '.'` over whole directories as a file-listing substitute, repeated README searches, and made two failed calls. The tester also ran the test suite about twelve times, including a pointless `cd /tmp`. The biggest process gap is that the reviewer finished (line 164 git_diff, approval by 23:05) before the tester added ~250 lines of test code, so the tester's additions were never reviewed. The same gap let 'table-driven tests' be claimed in the PR body when auth_test.go isn't table-driven. No reviewer or tester flagged the deploy-manifest issues. Judge verdicts caused no thrash; the weak merge_gate score on the tester's result (line 300) was not acted on.

findings.summary: The ask agent ran `search` with pattern '.' across entire directories (internal/collector, deploy/k8s twice, cmd), dumping every line instead of using list_files or list_symbols.
findings.evidence: Line 3: search {pattern: '.', path: 'deploy/k8s'}. Line 5: search {pattern: '.', path: 'internal/collector'} (1227ms, returns every line of store/partition.go etc.). Line 18: search {pattern: '.', path: 'cmd'}. Line 40: search {pattern: '.', path: 'deploy/k8s', glob: '*.yaml'}, a repeat of line 3.

findings.summary: The ask agent searched README.md three times with overlapping regexes (plus a no-match yaml-path search) before simply reading the relevant window.
findings.evidence: Line 41: search 'HTTP_ADDR|RETENTION_DAYS|env var|ConfigMap|...' in README.md. Line 43: search 'HTTP_ADDR|DB_PATH|RETENTION_DAYS|Configuration|...' returns no matches. Line 46: search 'RETENTION_DAYS|HTTP_ADDR|Collector Configuration|...'. Line 50 then does read_file README.md offset 92, which answered the question. The loop_control judge at line 47 rated repeating_itself 0.59.

findings.summary: The ask agent made failed calls against a nonexistent docs/ path and used list_symbols on a directory.
findings.evidence: Line 48: search {path: 'docs'} -> 'error: rg failed'. Line 19: list_symbols {path: 'internal/collector/ui'} -> 'error: not a file'. Line 59: remember {path: 'deploy/k8s'} -> 'error: missing file'.

findings.summary: The coder re-read internal/collector/ingest/http.go, a file it never edits and whose facts were already in its brief, despite the orchestrator saying 'already verified — do not re-derive'.
findings.evidence: Line 66 (orchestrator coder spec): 'FACTS (from a repo survey, already verified — do not re-derive, just use)'. Line 94: coder read_file internal/collector/ingest/http.go (full 94 lines), reasoning 'check README lines and ingest/http.go quickly'. The file is absent from the diff. The other re-reads, at lines 68, 70, 81, 82, 84 and 86, are justified by read-before-edit.

findings.summary: The reviewer took its diff snapshot and approved before the tester added ~250 lines of tests, so the tester's changes to three test files, which ship in the PR, were never reviewed.
findings.evidence: Line 164: reviewer git_diff runs right after the coder finished, and the reviewer approves at 23:05:16 ('verdict: approve'). The tester's str_replace edits come later: line 232 (forwarder_test.go), line 238 (auth_test.go), line 244 (collector_test.go). The tester finished at 23:07:53, and the orchestrator opened the PR without any re-review.

findings.summary: The coder described auth_test.go as 'table-style tests', and this carried through to the reviewer and the final PR body ('New table-driven tests cover both middlewares'), but the file it created is a series of standalone test functions.
findings.evidence: Line 130: create_file internal/collector/auth_test.go contains TestBasicAuthMiddlewareNoopWhenAuthDisabled, ...RejectsMissingCredentials, ...RejectsWrongCredentials, etc., with no table. The coder's report says 'auth_test.go (new): table-style tests per middleware'. The reviewer repeats 'tests follow existing table-driven convention', and the PR body claims table-driven tests.

findings.summary: The tester ran the full suite five times and targeted subsets seven more times, often with nothing changed in between, and its closing runs only confirmed earlier results.
findings.evidence: Full `go test ./...` runs at lines 202, 250, 263, 281 and 294 (the last three with no source edits between them except the gofmt fix at 255). Targeted runs at 217, 220, 223, 227, 277, 287 and 291, where lines 287 and 291 re-run the same '-run "Auth|Token|Protect"' filter just to reformat output. Reasoning at 294: 'let me do one final comprehensive test to make absolutely sure'.

findings.summary: The tester ran `cd /tmp && pwd`, which has nothing to do with the test plan and leaves the workspace; its reasoning says it was trying to 'verify the directory structure'.
findings.evidence: Line 193: run_command 'cd /tmp && pwd' -> '/tmp'. The exec_approval judge at line 192 rated escapes_workspace 0.48. The next call (line 194) is runtime_info, reasoning 'Let me check the current working directory'.

findings.summary: The tester's own edit to collector_test.go broke gofmt. It caught this only because it read the output, since `make fmt` (gofmt -l) exits 0 even when files are listed. It recovered correctly.
findings.evidence: Line 253: 'make vet && make fmt' exit code 0, stdout 'gofmt -l .\ninternal/collector/collector_test.go'. Line 255: 'gofmt -w internal/collector/collector_test.go'. Line 260: 'make fmt' clean. The coder had likewise guarded against the exit-0 behaviour with an explicit 'gofmt -l . ; echo exit=$?' at line 154.

findings.summary: The coder piped `go test ./...` through `| tail -80`, so the reported exit code is tail's and would have been 0 even if tests failed. The output did show every package passing, so there was no harm this time.
findings.evidence: Line 146: command 'go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -80' -> 'exit code: 0', stdout lists 'ok' for every tested package including internal/collector and internal/agent/forwarder.

findings.summary: The merge_gate judge scored the tester's result weakly (accomplished_its_brief 0.45, contradicts_siblings 0.24, worth_parent_context confidence 0.0), and the orchestrator went straight to the PR without looking into it.
findings.evidence: Line 300: merge_gate {accomplished_its_brief: 0.45, contradicts_siblings: 0.24, worth_parent_context: {score: 1.26, confidence: 0.0}}. The tester's transcript outcome begins 'Perfect! Everything is correctly implemented. Now let me create a final summary document:', a garbled lead-in. The orchestrator's next message says both agents found 'no issues' and offers to merge/PR.

findings.summary: The reviewer read the new Secret template and the diff's manifest changes but didn't notice the non-optional secret references or the 'changeme' template being swept up by the README's apply-glob, and it repeated the incorrect 'harmless no-op' claim as fact.
findings.evidence: Line 180: reviewer read_file deploy/k8s/collector-secret.yaml. Its report states 'agent-daemonset pulls AUTH_INGEST_TOKEN from the same Secret key, with a comment that it's a harmless no-op when auth disabled' and ends with 'verdict: approve'. Its only leftover was not being able to run tests.

strengths: The auth middleware is small and idiomatic: constant-time comparison, WWW-Authenticate only on Basic, separate ingest credential, no-op when disabled.
Fail-fast validation in collector.New stops AUTH_ENABLED=true with empty credentials, and it's covered by a table-driven test.
Health, ready and metrics endpoints are correctly left open for probes and scrapers, with a wiring-level test confirming it.
The agent side (config -> agent.go -> forwarder header) is threaded through cleanly and tested.
go test ./..., make vet and make fmt really ran and passed in the trace, after the last edit.
No read-before-edit violations; the coder's work was tight and sequential, driven by a precise orchestrator spec.
concerns: Non-optional secretKeyRef/secretRef means pods fail to start without the Secret even when auth is disabled, contradicting the 'opt-in' framing.
A 'changeme' credentials Secret lives inside the deploy/k8s/*.yaml apply glob.
AUTH_ENABLED fails open on values ParseBool doesn't accept.
The explicitly requested table-driven convention wasn't followed in auth_test.go, and the PR body says otherwise.
The reviewer approved before the tester's ~250 lines of test additions existed, so those changes shipped unreviewed.
The tester re-ran the suite far more than needed, and the ask agent wasted calls on directory-dump searches.
overall_assessment.narrative: The engine produced a clean, well-scoped Go implementation, and the coder's part of the run was efficient and disciplined: it read before editing, ran the required checks and verified output, not just exit codes. The weak spots come from the verification stage. The reviewer ran in parallel with the tester, approved a snapshot that didn't yet include the tester's test changes, and like the tester it accepted the coder's own claims ('harmless no-op', 'table-driven') without checking the deploy manifests or test structure against them. As a result, a handful of real but easily fixed issues reached the PR: fail-closed pod startup when the Secret is missing, a changeme Secret in the apply glob, a fail-open boolean parse, and the test style mismatch. Fix those and the PR is mergeable. On the process side, the main lesson is to serialize the reviewer after the tester, or have it re-review after the tester's edits.
